1	# HTTP Request Node — Implementation
2	
3	This page is the entry point for implementing a managed HTTP node. Pick your auth mode below, then follow the matching walkthrough end-to-end. The "Shared Reference" section is an appendix — the mode walkthroughs already inline what you need to act, and link here only for full rationale and extended examples.
4	
5	## Node Type
6	
7	`core.action.http.v2` (Managed HTTP Request)
8	
9	> **Always use `core.action.http.v2`** for all HTTP requests. The older `core.action.http` (v1) is deprecated.
10	
11	## Pick a Mode
12	
13	| Mode | Use when | Walkthrough |
14	| --- | --- | --- |
15	| **Connector** | Target system has an IS connector — auth via an existing IS connection (OAuth/API key) | [impl-connector.md](impl-connector.md) |
16	| **Manual** | No connector exists, public/no-auth API, or quick prototyping | [impl-manual.md](impl-manual.md) |
17	
18	> **Mode fallback — auto-try, then confirm.** Prefer a curated connector activity first; if none, use connector mode; if connector mode cannot be configured (connector lacks HTTP request support — `HasHttpRequest` false — or no usable IS connection), fall through to manual mode automatically. Manual changes the auth model (you supply auth yourself), so confirm the switched mode with the user before finalizing. See [impl-connector.md — Step 2](impl-connector.md#step-2--identify-target-connection).
19	
20	The `--detail` payload differs in two places between modes: `authentication` (`"connector"` vs `"manual"`), and the connector-binding fields `targetConnector` / `connectionId` / `folderKey` (connector mode only; `url` is then relative to the connector base, vs. an absolute URL in manual mode). Everything else (node add, dynamic values, branches, edges, debug) is shared.
21	
22	## Critical: Use `node configure`
23	
24	> **Do not hand-write `inputs.detail`, `bindings_v2.json`, or connection resource files.** Run `uip maestro flow node configure` — it builds everything from a simple `--detail` JSON. Hand-written configurations miss the `essentialConfiguration` block and fail at runtime. `core.action.http.v2` is CLI-owned per [Author capability — Node ownership](../../../CAPABILITY.md#node-ownership--who-authors-the-node) (same envelope rules as connector activities).
25	
26	## Registry validation
27	
28	```bash
29	uip maestro flow registry get core.action.http.v2 --output json
30	```
31	
32	Confirm in `Data.Node.handleConfiguration`: target port `input`, source ports `branch-{item.id}` (dynamic, `repeat: inputs.branches`) and `default`. Also confirm `Data.Node.supportsErrorHandling: true` — HTTP v2 participates in the implicit `error` port pattern shared by every action node (see [Action Node Structure](../../../../shared/action-nodes.md)). Model `serviceType` is `Intsvc.UnifiedHttpRequest`.
33	
34	---
35	
36	## Shared Reference (appendix)
37	
38	The mode walkthroughs link into the sections below for full rationale and extended examples. You do not need to read this section in order — jump directly from the walkthrough link that brought you here.
39	
40	### Add the node
41	
42	```bash
43	uip maestro flow node add <ProjectName>.flow core.action.http.v2 \
44	  --label "<HTTP node label>" --output json
45	```
46	
47	The CLI copies the manifest into `definitions[]`, adds the node instance to `nodes[]`, registers the `variables.nodes` entries, and inserts a placeholder in `layout.nodes` — all in code, byte-for-byte from the registry (including `typeVersion`, which the CLI pulls from the manifest's `version` field; do not hardcode it). Save the returned node ID — both walkthroughs reuse it.
48	
49	The CLI initializes `inputs` from the manifest's `inputDefaults`:
50	
51	```json
52	"inputs": {
53	  "branches": [],
54	  "timeout": "PT15M",
55	  "retryCount": 0,
56	  "swaggerDefinition": null,
57	  "detail": {}
58	}
59	```
60	
61	`inputs.detail` is populated by the configure step (next). The inputs-level siblings — `branches`, `timeout`, `retryCount` — are set at `node add` time via `--input`:
62	
63	```bash
64	uip maestro flow node add <ProjectName>.flow core.action.http.v2 \
65	  --label "<HTTP node label>" \
66	  --input '{
67	    "timeout": "PT30M",
68	    "retryCount": 3,
69	    "branches": [
70	      { "id": "hasItems", "name": "Has Items", "conditionExpression": "$self.output.body.items.length > 0" },
71	      { "id": "empty",    "name": "Empty",    "conditionExpression": "$self.output.body.items.length == 0" }
72	    ]
73	  }' --output json
74	```
75	
76	- `timeout` — ISO 8601 duration (e.g. `PT15M`, `PT1H`, `P1D`). Default `PT15M`.
77	- `retryCount` — integer. Default `0`.
78	- `branches` — see [Conditional branches](#conditional-branches) below.
79	
80	> **Do not hand-author the `core.action.http.v2` definition, and do not `Edit` `inputs.*` after the fact.** Use `uip maestro flow node add` (with `--input` for branches/timeout/retryCount) and `uip maestro flow node configure` (for `inputs.detail`). These are the only supported authoring paths.
81	
82	### Dynamic values in URL / headers / body / query
83	
84	**IS activity input fields do not resolve `{$vars.x}` brace-templates.** The flow runtime's `{...}` template interpolation only applies to native flow fields (end-node output `source`, variable updates, decision `expression`, script body, etc.) — **not** to fields under `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` on HTTP v2 or on any `uipath.connector.*` activity. Evidence: `"url": "https://.../user/{$vars.article}/..."` ships to the service as literal `{vars.article}` (the `$` is stripped, braces remain), producing a 400 Bad Request.
85	
86	**Use `=js:` expressions for any dynamic value in IS activity inputs.** The runtime evaluates `=js:` before handing the value to the connector:
87	
88	```json
89	"bodyParameters": {
90	  "url": "=js:`https://api.example.com/users/${$vars.userId}/orders`",
91	  "headers": {
92	    "Authorization": "=js:'Bearer ' + $vars.apiToken",
93	    "X-Request-ID": "=js:$metadata.instanceId"
94	  },
95	  "query": {
96	    "since": "=js:$vars.startDate"
97	  }
98	}
99	```
100	
101	Template literals with `${...}` interpolation work because the whole expression is evaluated as JavaScript — `$vars` is a global in the `=js:` context. Plain string concatenation (`'Bearer ' + $vars.token`) works the same way.
102	
103	When calling `uip maestro flow node configure --detail`, pass the `=js:` string verbatim — the CLI stores it in `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` unchanged:
104	
105	```bash
106	uip maestro flow node configure <Project>.flow <nodeId> \
107	  --detail '{
108	    "authentication": "manual",
109	    "method": "GET",
110	    "url": "=js:`https://api.example.com/users/${$vars.userId}`"
111	  }' --output json
112	```
113	
114	### Conditional branches
115	
116	Skip this section unless you need to route downstream paths based on the *response content* (e.g., `items.length > 0` vs empty). Do **not** use `branches` just to handle call failures — for that, use the `error` port (see [Wire edges](#wire-edges)).
117	
118	Each branch entry creates a `branch-{id}` source port. `$self` refers to the current HTTP node's output inside the condition.
119	
120	Set `branches` at `node add` time via `--input` (see [Add the node](#add-the-node)) — `branches` lives at `inputs.branches`, not `inputs.detail.branches`, and `node configure --detail` does not accept it.
121	
122	```bash
123	uip maestro flow node add <ProjectName>.flow core.action.http.v2 \
124	  --label "<HTTP node label>" \
125	  --input '{
126	    "branches": [
127	      { "id": "hasItems", "name": "Has Items", "conditionExpression": "$self.output.body.items.length > 0" },
128	      { "id": "empty",    "name": "Empty",    "conditionExpression": "$self.output.body.items.length == 0" }
129	    ]
130	  }' --output json
131	```
132	
133	> **Do not prefix `conditionExpression` with `=js:`** — HTTP branch conditions are auto-evaluated as JS (same rule as decision/switch expressions).
134	
135	### Wire edges
136	
137	The managed HTTP node's target port is `input`. Its source ports are:
138	
139	- `default` — primary success output (or fallback when configured branches don't match)
140	- `error` — fires when the HTTP call fails (network error, timeout, non-2xx not caught by a branch); wire this to an error handler to keep the flow from faulting
141	- `branch-{id}` — one per entry in `inputs.branches` ([Conditional branches](#conditional-branches)); use the exact `id` you set
142	
143	Use `Edit` to add edge objects to `edges[]`; do not use `uip maestro flow edge add` for this structural wiring. Examples:
144	
145	```json
146	{
147	  "id": "e-<upstreamNodeId>-<nodeId>",
148	  "sourceNodeId": "<upstreamNodeId>",
149	  "sourcePort": "<port>",
150	  "targetNodeId": "<nodeId>",
151	  "targetPort": "input"
152	}
153	```
154	
155	```json
156	{
157	  "id": "e-<nodeId>-<downstreamNodeId>",
158	  "sourceNodeId": "<nodeId>",
159	  "sourcePort": "default",
160	  "targetNodeId": "<downstreamNodeId>",
161	  "targetPort": "input"
162	}
163	```
164	
165	```json
166	{
167	  "id": "e-<nodeId>-<errorHandlerId>",
168	  "sourceNodeId": "<nodeId>",
169	  "sourcePort": "error",
170	  "targetNodeId": "<errorHandlerId>",
171	  "targetPort": "input"
172	}
173	```
174	
175	Add the `error` edge above **only when the requirements say what should happen if the call fails.** With no error edge, a failed call faults the flow — the correct, visible default.
176	
177	When an HTTP node does have an outgoing `error` edge, the HTTP node instance must also include `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true`. `uip maestro flow edge add --source-port error` and `uip maestro flow format` set this automatically; direct JSON edits must set it explicitly. Never set the flag on an HTTP node with no error edge — it suppresses the fault, so a failed call flows on and the run reports success. See [file-format.md — Default: off](../../../../shared/file-format.md#default-off--enable-only-for-a-failure-the-flow-actually-handles).
178	
179	```json
180	{
181	  "id": "e-<nodeId>-<hasItemsDownstream>",
182	  "sourceNodeId": "<nodeId>",
183	  "sourcePort": "branch-hasItems",
184	  "targetNodeId": "<hasItemsDownstream>",
185	  "targetPort": "input"
186	}
187	```
188	
189	### Debug
190	
191	| Error | Cause | Fix |
192	| --- | --- | --- |
193	| `not_authed` or 401/403 | Wrong node type (v1 instead of v2), missing bindings, or expired connection | Verify node type is `core.action.http.v2`, check `bindings_v2.json` exists, ping the connection |
194	| `configuration` field missing | Node not configured via CLI | Run `uip maestro flow node configure` — do not hand-write `inputs.detail` |
195	| `flow validate` errors with `uiPathActivityTypeId` missing on `core.action.http.v2` | Node was hand-authored in `definitions[]` instead of via `uip maestro flow node add` | Remove the node, re-add it via `uip maestro flow node add <file> core.action.http.v2 ...`, then re-run `node configure`. |
196	| Connection not found | Wrong connection ID or connector key | Re-run `uip is connections list` for the target connector |
197	| Wrong API response | Incorrect `url` or `query` | Check the target service's API documentation |
198	| `ImplicitConnection` errors | Manual mode misconfigured | Verify `authentication: "manual"` and `url` is a full URL |
199	| Flow faults on 4xx/5xx response | No `error` edge wired from the HTTP node | Expected when the requirements specify no fallback. If they do, add an edge with `sourcePort: "error"` to an error-handler node. See [Implicit error port on action nodes](../../../../shared/file-format.md#implicit-error-port-on-action-nodes) — same mechanism applies to all action nodes |
200	| Flow reports `Completed` but the API call failed | `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true` with no handler, or an `error` edge routed into the happy path / the success End node | Remove the flag when there is no error edge; otherwise repoint the error edge at a distinct End node with an error/status output, or at `core.logic.terminate`. See [Do not swallow the failure](../../../../shared/file-format.md#do-not-swallow-the-failure) |
201	| Edge `source-port output` rejected | Referencing the variable namespace as a port name | HTTP source ports are `default`, `error`, and `branch-{id}` — not `output`. The `output` name is only a variable namespace (`$vars.{nodeId}.output`) |

1	# UiPath Flow File Format
2	
3	The `.flow` file is a JSON document at `<ProjectName>.flow` in the project root. It is the **only file you should edit** — other generated files will be overwritten.
4	
5	## Table of contents
6	
7	- [Top-level structure](#top-level-structure)
8	- [Project structure (generated scaffold)](#project-structure-generated-scaffold)
9	- [Node instance](#node-instance)
10	- [Layout](#layout)
11	- [Edge — both ports required](#edge--both-ports-required)
12	- [Definition entry](#definition-entry)
13	- [Common node types](#common-node-types)
14	- [Standard ports by node type](#standard-ports-by-node-type)
15	- [Implicit error port on action nodes](#implicit-error-port-on-action-nodes)
16	- [Minimal working example — dice roller](#minimal-working-example--dice-roller)
17	- [entry-points.json — auto-generated, do not edit](#entry-pointsjson--auto-generated-do-not-edit)
18	- [Bindings — Orchestrator resource bindings (top-level `bindings[]`)](#bindings--orchestrator-resource-bindings-top-level-bindings)
19	- [Bindings — connector connection binding](#bindings--connector-connection-binding)
20	
21	## Top-level structure
22	
23	```json
24	{
25	  "id": "<uuid>",
26	  "version": "<scaffolded file-format version>",
27	  "name": "MyFlow",
28	  "nodes": [],
29	  "edges": [],
30	  "definitions": [],
31	  "bindings": [],
32	  "variables": {},
33	  "layout": {
34	    "nodes": {}
35	  }
36	}
37	```
38	
39	> **Key order is NOT guaranteed — never anchor edits on it.** The skeleton above is illustrative; the CLI does not commit to a stable top-level key sequence or to which optional keys are present. Real flows vary: `runtime` may appear (and has been observed *before* `nodes`, not after `definitions`) or be absent entirely; `bindings`, `variables`, `solutionId`, `projectId`, and a trailing `metadata` object surface in different positions depending on CLI version and what the flow contains. When editing a `.flow`, anchor each `Edit` on the **target array's own key** (`"nodes": [`, `"edges": [`, `"definitions": [`, or `layout.nodes`) located in the text you just `Read` — never on "the key that follows X." See [greenfield.md — Anchoring parallel `.flow` Edits](../author/references/greenfield.md#anchoring-parallel-flow-edits--anchor-on-what-you-read-not-on-key-order).
40	
41	Optional top-level `runtime`: a CLI-managed object that appears on some flows (e.g. after `uip maestro flow node add` for an HTTP/connector node) and is absent on others. It is not user-authored — do not add, remove, or anchor on it. Its presence and position are not guaranteed.
42	
43	<!--skill-flavor:flow-format-version-source:start-->
44	**Top-level `version`** = workflow file-format version. **Use the exact value `uip maestro flow init` scaffolds** — do not hand-pick, hardcode, or downgrade it. It is not a semver string; the schema gates on an exact literal for the current file-format version, so an older value (e.g. `"1.0"`, `"1.0.0"`) that worked for a legacy parser will fail for a new flow. `init` always writes the accepted value; preserve it. To see the current value, scaffold a throwaway flow with `init` and read its top-level `version`, or read it from an existing `init`-generated `.flow`.
45	<!--skill-flavor:flow-format-version-source:end-->
46	
47	> **Don't confuse top-level `version` with `definitions[].version` / `typeVersion`.** Node-definition `version` (and matching node-instance `typeVersion`) are validated by `versionSchema`, a regex that accepts both `x.y` and `x.y.z` (`/^\d+\.\d+(\.\d+)?$/`, error `'Version must be in format "x.y" or "x.y.z"'`). Both layers are canonically `x.y`, but the node-level regex still accepts legacy 3-part strings so registry definitions (`"1.0"`) and older scaffolded nodes (`"1.0.0"`) both parse. The two layers report distinct errors, but Zod may collapse a node-level mismatch to path `(root)`. If you see a version-related error at `(root)`, audit the top-level `version` first; if it's correct, check each node's `typeVersion` against the matching `definitions[].version`.
48	
49	`solutionId` and `projectId` may also appear at the top level — these are auto-populated by the project scaffold and packaging. Preserve the generated values.
50	
51	> **`bindings[]`** holds Orchestrator resource references for `uipath.core.*` resource nodes (rpa, agent, flow, agentic-process, api-workflow, hitl) and for connector-node connections. See [Bindings — Orchestrator resource bindings](#bindings--orchestrator-resource-bindings-top-level-bindings) below and the [connector plugin](../author/references/plugins/connector/impl.md) for the connector-binding shape.
52	
53	## Project structure (generated scaffold)
54	
55	```
56	<ProjectName>/
57	├── project.uiproj          # { "Name": "...", "ProjectType": "Flow" }
58	├── <ProjectName>.flow      # ← edit this
59	├── bindings_v2.json        # resource bindings
60	├── entry-points.json       # input/output schema declarations
61	├── operate.json            # runtime options
62	└── package-descriptor.json # packaging manifest
63	```
64	
65	## Node instance
66	
67	```json
68	{
69	  "id": "rollDice",
70	  "type": "core.action.script",
71	  "typeVersion": "1.0",
72	  "display": { "label": "Roll Dice" },
73	  "inputs": {
74	    "script": "return { roll: Math.floor(Math.random() * 6) + 1 };"
75	  },
76	  "outputs": {
77	    "output": {
78	      "type": "object",
79	      "description": "The return value of the script",
80	      "source": "=result.response",
81	      "var": "output"
82	    },
83	    "error": {
84	      "type": "object",
85	      "description": "Error information if the script fails",
86	      "source": "=Error",
87	      "var": "error"
88	    }
89	  }
90	}
91	```
92	
93	**Required fields on every node**: `id`, `type`, `typeVersion`, **`display`** (with at least a `label`). This applies to **every** node — triggers (`core.trigger.manual`, `core.trigger.scheduled`, connector triggers), action nodes, control-flow nodes (`core.control.end`, `core.logic.terminate`), and human-task nodes. The Zod `nodeSchema` declares `display: displayConfigSchema` without `.optional()`, so no node type is exempt — even ones that "feel" trivial.
94	
95	`typeVersion` must match the corresponding `definitions[].version` exactly. The registry often returns versions such as `"1.0"` while older examples or scaffolded files may show `"1.0.0"`. If a node uses `typeVersion: "1.0.0"` but the copied definition is `"version": "1.0"`, validation reports "Node type `<type>:1.0.0` has no matching definition." When direct-authoring a new node from `registry get`, set `typeVersion` to the copied definition's `version`; when preserving an existing node, preserve its existing node/definition pair unless you intentionally update both together. <!-- version-check-skip --> (explains the x.y vs x.y.z mismatch mechanic; literals are illustrative, not pinned)
96	
97	> **Gotcha — vague schema-validation error on missing `display`.** Omitting `display` on any node produces:
98	>
99	> ```
100	> [error] [(root)] Schema validation failed: Invalid input: expected object, received undefined
101	> ```
102	>
103	> The error path is `(root)` and does NOT pinpoint which node or which field is missing. If you see this error after editing a `.flow` file, audit every node for a `display` block before doing anything else.
104	
105	> **No instance `model` block.** BPMN type, serviceType, event definition, and binding/context templates all live in the node's **definition** (the manifest copied from the registry into `definitions[]`). The runtime hydrates them from the definition at serialization time — instances carry only per-instance data (`inputs`, `outputs`, `display`). This applies to every inline-agent-related node too: `uipath.agent.autonomous` plus every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node (tool, escalation, context) carries source identity at `inputs.source`. Their definitions declare `model.source: true`; flow-core hoists that identity onto each instance's `inputs.source`. Do not write a `"model": { "source": ... }` block on the instance.
106	>
107	> **No `ui` block on nodes.** Position and size are stored in the top-level `layout` object, not on individual nodes. See [Layout](#layout) below.
108	
109	### Instance-specific identity fields
110	
111	A few per-instance identity fields live on the node instance:
112	
113	| Field | Used by | Purpose |
114	|-------|---------|---------|
115	| `inputs.entryPointId` | All trigger nodes (`core.trigger.manual`, `core.trigger.scheduled`, connector triggers) | Stable UUID identifying the entry point |
116	| `inputs.isDefaultEntryPoint` | Trigger nodes in subflows | Boolean marking the default entry point when a subflow has multiple triggers |
117	| `inputs.source` | `uipath.agent.autonomous` and every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node (tool, escalation, context) | For `uipath.agent.autonomous`: the inline agent's `projectId`. For resource nodes: the attached resource UUID. Definitions declare `model.source: true`; flow-core hoists onto the instance — no instance `model` block. |
118	| `inputs.color`, `inputs.content` | Sticky-note nodes | Visual content of the sticky note |

124	  "id": "start",
125	  "type": "core.trigger.manual",
126	  "typeVersion": "1.0",
127	  "display": { "label": "Manual trigger" },
128	  "inputs": {
129	    "entryPointId": "3d4a8c34-5682-4ebe-a6bc-d92a18830bb5"
130	  },
131	  "outputs": {
132	    "output": { "type": "object", "description": "Data passed when manually triggering the process.", "source": "null", "var": "output" }
133	  }

136	
137	### Node outputs
138	
139	`$vars.<sourceNodeId>.<outputId>` resolution at runtime is driven by **`variables.nodes[]`**, not by the node instance's `outputs` block. The BPMN emitter walks `variables.nodes[]` to write the process-level `<uipath:inputOutput id="<nodeId>.<outputId>">` declarations the runtime needs; the action-node instance `outputs` block is ignored at serialization (the manifest's `outputDefinition` supplies the activity-side mapping). End / terminate nodes are the exception — their instance `outputs` block IS consumed to map workflow-level `out` variables. See [end/impl.md](../author/references/plugins/end/impl.md).
140	
141	The canonical recipe for a data-producing node is therefore:
142	
143	- `definitions[]` entry copied verbatim from `uip maestro flow registry get` (carries the manifest `outputDefinition`).
144	- `variables.nodes[]` entry per output: `{ "id": "<nodeId>.<outputId>", "type": "object", "binding": { "nodeId": "<nodeId>", "outputId": "<outputId>" } }`.
145	- Optional instance `outputs` block matching the manifest — harmless and matches the canonical examples below for clarity, but **not** what controls runtime variable visibility.
146	
147	Skipping `variables.nodes[]` produces a flow that passes `flow validate` but resolves `$vars.<sourceNodeId>.output` to `undefined` at runtime (MST-9972). `uip maestro flow format` regenerates `variables.nodes[]` from `nodes[]` + `definitions[]`, so always run it after structural edits — the omission becomes self-healing.
148	
149	When you DO author the instance `outputs` block (for documentation / parity with manifest schema), use the shape below. Each output entry has:
150	
151	- `type` — data type (usually `"object"`)
152	- `description` — human-readable description
153	- `source` — runtime binding expression, copied from the manifest `outputDefinition`. `"=Error"` for errors, always.
154	- `var` — the variable name (matches the output ID, e.g., `"output"`, `"error"`)
155	
156	**Orchestrator-job nodes (api-workflow, rpa-workflow, agent, agentic-process, function): declare `error` only — `output` is derived.** They are the one family whose instance block the converter reads: it copies an authored `source` verbatim, and injects `{output, jsonSchema, "=this"}` when a non-empty `outputs` omits `output`. So `"=result.response"` there — the connector/script source — leaves `$vars.<nodeId>.output` null at runtime while `flow validate` passes. Studio Web serializes `error`-only instances too (verified on api-workflow, published-flow, and inline-agent nodes). Subflow and published-flow (`uipath.core.flow.*`) instance blocks are never read — still declare `error` only.
157	
158	The standard `outputs` block for most action nodes (script, HTTP, transform, connector):
159	
160	```json
161	"outputs": {
162	  "output": {
163	    "type": "object",
164	    "description": "The return value of the <node type>",
165	    "source": "=result.response",
166	    "var": "output"
167	  },
168	  "error": {
169	    "type": "object",
170	    "description": "Error information if the <node type> fails",
171	    "source": "=Error",
172	    "var": "error"
173	  }
174	}
175	```
176	
177	Trigger nodes (manual, scheduled, connector triggers) have a single output — no error port. A manual trigger carries the literal string `"null"` as its `source`, matching what Studio Web writes:
178	
179	```json
180	"outputs": {
181	  "output": {
182	    "type": "object",
183	    "description": "Data passed when manually triggering the process.",
184	    "source": "null",
185	    "var": "output"
186	  }
187	}
188	```
189	
190	End/terminate nodes do **not** use this pattern — their `outputs` maps workflow-level output variables (see the [Author end plugin reference](../author/references/plugins/end/impl.md)).
191	
192	## Layout
193	
194	Node positioning is stored in a **top-level `layout` object**, keyed by node `id`. The same shape applies inside each subflow as `subflows[<id>].layout`. Layout data is owned by `uip maestro flow format` (see [cli-commands.md](cli-commands.md#uip-maestro-flow-format)) — you should not need to hand-write it.
195	
196	```json
197	"layout": {
198	  "nodes": {
199	    "start": {
200	      "position": { "x": 200, "y": 144 },
201	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
202	      "collapsed": false
203	    },
204	    "rollDice": {
205	      "position": { "x": 400, "y": 144 },
206	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
207	      "collapsed": false
208	    },
209	    "end": {
210	      "position": { "x": 600, "y": 144 },
211	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
212	      "collapsed": false
213	    }
214	  }
215	}
216	```
217	
218	Each key in `layout.nodes` is a node `id`. `flow format` creates an entry for every node and populates `position` + `size`.
219	
220	**What format does:**
221	- Arranges nodes horizontally (left-to-right) with `nodeSpacing: 96`, anchored to the leftmost node's original position
222	- Sets each node's `size` to match its canvas shape: inline agents (`uipath.agent.autonomous` / `uipath.agent.conversational`, `shape: rectangle`) → `{ "width": 288, "height": 96 }`; containers (loops/groups) → `{ "width": 560, "height": 320 }`; everything else — including referenced `uipath.core.agent.<guid>` nodes — → `{ "width": 96, "height": 96 }`. A size that disagrees with the node's shape renders misshapen in Studio Web.
223	- Skips `stickyNote` nodes from layout (they keep their custom position and size)
224	- Recurses into every subflow and rewrites its `subflows[<id>].layout` map
225	
226	**Script:** `python3 scripts/check_runtime_gaps.py <flow>` reports nodes whose `layout` entry is missing or whose `size` disagrees with the shape sizes above — the MST-9061 symptom — without rewriting anything; `uip maestro flow format` remains the fix.
227	
228	**Subflow layout is scoped.** Each subflow entry in `subflows[<id>]` has its **own** `layout.nodes` map for the nodes inside that subflow — they do NOT live in the top-level `layout.nodes`. Format handles both passes. See the [Author subflow plugin reference](../author/references/plugins/subflow/impl.md).
229	
230	## Edge — both ports required
231	
232	```json
233	{
234	  "id": "edge-start-rollDice",
235	  "sourceNodeId": "start",
236	  "sourcePort": "output",
237	  "targetNodeId": "rollDice",
238	  "targetPort": "input"
239	}
240	```
241	
242	> **Gotcha**: `targetPort` is required. Omitting it produces `[error] [edges[N].targetPort] Invalid input: expected string, received undefined` at validate time.
243	>
244	> **Gotcha**: the source field is `sourcePort`, not `sourceHandle`. If you write `sourceHandle`, validation fails with `[error] [edges[N].sourcePort] Invalid input: expected string, received undefined` — the path identifies the offending edge entry exactly.
245	>
246	> **Gotcha — edge `id` MUST start with a letter (XML NCName).** Never use a bare UUID or any id with a leading digit (`"12bd09dd-…"`, `"1edge-start"`). Edge ids become BPMN `<bpmn:incoming>/<bpmn:outgoing>` IDREFs; a leading digit makes the converter silently drop those references while still emitting the `sequenceFlow`, so `flow validate` passes and upload succeeds — but the engine cannot traverse: the run reports **Completed having executed only the start node**, every output null. Use descriptive ids (`e-<source>-<target>`, e.g. `e-start-agent`); prefixing a letter (`e12bd09dd-…`) also works. Same rule applies to node ids.

308	## Implicit error port on action nodes
309	
310	Any node with `supportsErrorHandling: true` in the registry exposes an implicit `error` source port for catching node-level failures. This applies to HTTP, Script, Transform (all variants), connector activities, agent nodes, and RPA nodes — essentially every action node.
311	
312	The port is **not** listed in the registry's `handleConfiguration`. Studio Web only exposes it when the source node has `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true`; when the flow contains an outgoing edge with `sourcePort: "error"` from that node, the serializer emits a BPMN boundary error event attached to the node. Because of this gate, `uip maestro flow validate` reports an error when a node has an outgoing `sourcePort: "error"` edge but `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled` is not `true` — so the inconsistency is caught before publish rather than surfacing as a hidden edge in Studio Web.
313	
314	### Default: off — enable only for a failure the flow actually handles
315	
316	`inputs.errorHandlingEnabled` is **opt-in, and stays off unless the requirements name a failure fallback.** Turning it on suppresses the node's fault: the node returns instead of faulting and execution continues. Enable it only when both hold:
317	
318	1. The requirements state what should happen when this node fails ("if the call fails, …", "return X for invalid input", "handle timeouts") — **and**
319	2. You wire the node's `error` port to a handler that produces an outcome distinguishable from success.
320	
321	Never set the flag on a node that has no outgoing `error` edge — it suppresses the fault with nothing to catch it, converting a real failure into a run that reports success. Let the CLI own the flag: `uip maestro flow edge add --source-port error` and `uip maestro flow format` set it from the error edges actually present. If you find the flag on a node with no error edge, remove it.
322	
323	### Do not swallow the failure
324	
325	An `error` edge must not rejoin the happy path. When it does, every failure walks the success route and the run reports `Completed` while the work never happened — the flow "always looks successful."
326	
327	| | Error-path target | Result |
328	| --- | --- | --- |
329	| ✗ | The next node on the happy path | Failure is invisible; downstream nodes run on missing data |
330	| ✗ | The same End node the success path reaches | Success path's output mappings run against the failed node's empty output |
331	| ✓ | A **distinct** End node mapping an error/status `out` variable | Caller can tell failure from success |
332	| ✓ | `core.logic.terminate` | Aborts the flow when recovery is impossible — see [terminate/impl.md](../author/references/plugins/terminate/impl.md) |
333	| ✓ | A recovery branch that rejoins **only after obtaining valid data** — a retry that succeeded, or a fallback source that returned data | Downstream runs on real data, not on the failed node's empty output |
334	
335	```text
336	Trigger -> HTTP Request
337	  |-- default -> Process -> End (success — status: "ok")
338	  |-- error   -> Log Error -> End (failure — status: "failed", message from $vars.httpCall.error)
339	```
340	
341	### When the error port fires
342	
343	- Network failures, DNS errors, TLS errors
344	- Request timeouts
345	- Non-2xx HTTP responses (unless caught by a configured `inputs.branches` entry)
346	- Script exceptions (`throw`, undefined reference, etc.)
347	- Transform operation failures (invalid collection, missing field)
348	- Any unhandled runtime exception inside the node
349	
350	Without a wired error edge, any of these fails the whole flow with `finalStatus: "Faulted"`. **That is the correct default, not a defect to design around** — a faulted run is visible to the operator; a swallowed failure is not. Only trade the fault for an error path when the requirements say what that path should do.
351	
352	### Wiring the error port
353	
354	```bash
355	# Confirm the node supports error handling
356	uip maestro flow registry get <node-type> --output json --output-filter "Node.SupportsErrorHandling"
357	
358	# Add an outgoing edge with sourcePort: "error"
359	uip maestro flow edge add <Project>.flow <actionNodeId> <errorHandlerId> \
360	  --source-port error --target-port input --output json
361	```
362	
363	`uip maestro flow edge add --source-port error` and `uip maestro flow format` set `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true` on the source node automatically — only for nodes that have an error edge. When editing `.flow` JSON directly, set the flag yourself **on those nodes only**:
364	
365	```json
366	{
367	  "id": "<actionNodeId>",
368	  "inputs": {
369	    "errorHandlingEnabled": true
370	  }
371	}
372	```
373	
374	Inside the error handler, `$vars.{actionNodeId}.error` resolves to the error object. For HTTP it's `{ code, message, detail, category, status }`; other nodes have similar shapes — check the node's `outputDefinition.error.schema` in the registry.
375	
376	### Error port vs other branching
377	
378	| Mechanism | When to use |
379	| --- | --- |
380	| **`error` source port** (any action node) | The node failed (exception, timeout, non-2xx not caught by a branch). Generic "something went wrong" handler. |
381	| **`branch-{id}` ports** (HTTP only, `inputs.branches`) | The call succeeded and you want to route on response *content* — different paths for e.g. empty vs non-empty results. |
382	| **`core.logic.decision` downstream** | Simple yes/no routing on the node's successful output. Doesn't help if the node itself fails. |
383	| **`core.logic.switch` downstream** | Multi-way routing on the node's successful output. Same — doesn't catch failures. |

490	### Step 2 — Populate definitions from the registry
491	
492	Run one command per node type used in `nodes`. Copy the returned node definition object from each response into the `definitions` array, and set each matching node instance's `typeVersion` to the copied definition's exact `version`.
493	
494	```bash
495	uip maestro flow registry get core.trigger.manual --output json
496	uip maestro flow registry get core.action.script --output json
497	uip maestro flow registry get core.logic.terminate --output json

500	The `definitions` array must contain exactly one entry per unique `type:typeVersion` used — not one per node instance. If two nodes share the same type and version, one definition covers both.

503	
504	## entry-points.json — auto-generated, do not edit
505	
506	`entry-points.json` declares the flow's external interface (input/output schemas and trigger entry points). Preserve its lifecycle-generated contents; project scaffolding creates it, and the Flow lifecycle regenerates it before execution or publication.
507	
508	Flow input and output parameters are declared through **variables** in the `.flow` file:
509	- **Flow inputs**: Add entries to `variables.nodes[]` whose `binding.nodeId` is the start node and whose `binding.outputId` names each input value — the start node "outputs" input values to downstream nodes
510	- **Flow outputs**: Add output variables to the end/terminate node
511	- Downstream nodes reference inputs via `$vars.start.output.<paramName>`
512	
513	The packaging/debug step derives `entry-points.json` from these variable declarations.
514	
515	## Bindings — Orchestrator resource bindings (top-level `bindings[]`)
516	
517	The top-level `bindings` array (a sibling of `nodes`, `edges`, `definitions`, `variables`, `layout`) holds resource-reference indirections for **Orchestrator resource nodes** — RPA workflows, agents, flows, agentic processes, API workflows, and HITL apps.
518	
519	Each resource node needs two binding entries (one for `name`, one for `folderPath`). The node instance itself has no binding or context data — just `inputs`. The definition (copied verbatim from the registry) carries `model.context[]` templates like `<bindings.name>` and `<bindings.folderPath>`. At BPMN emit time the runtime rewrites those placeholders to `=bindings.<id>` by matching the placeholder name against a workflow-level binding, scoped by the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey`.
520	
521	```json
522	"bindings": [
523	  {
524	    "id": "<UNIQUE_ID>",
525	    "name": "name",
526	    "type": "string",
527	    "resource": "process",
528	    "resourceKey": "<FolderPath>.<ResourceName>",
529	    "default": "<ResourceName>",
530	    "propertyAttribute": "name",
531	    "resourceSubType": "Process"
532	  },
533	  {
534	    "id": "<UNIQUE_ID_2>",
535	    "name": "folderPath",
536	    "type": "string",
537	    "resource": "process",
538	    "resourceKey": "<FolderPath>.<ResourceName>",
539	    "default": "<FolderPath>",
540	    "propertyAttribute": "folderPath",
541	    "resourceSubType": "Process"
542	  }
543	]
544	```
545	
546	**Rules:**
547	
548	- Add **two entries** per resource node (one for `name`, one for `folderPath`).
549	- **Share** entries across node instances that reference the same resource — do not duplicate. Matching is by `(resourceKey, name)`, so any node whose definition has the same `resourceKey` resolves to the same binding pair.
550	- Entry IDs are unique strings within the file. Descriptive IDs (e.g. `bDepositRpaName`) are preferred over short random IDs.
551	- The node instance has no `model` block — it carries only `inputs`, `outputs`, and `display`.
552	- `resourceKey` must exactly match the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey` (verbatim from the registry). The runtime uses this key to scope placeholder resolution so that binding names like `name` / `folderPath` (shared across resource kinds) don't cross-alias.
553	- `resourceSubType` mirrors the definition's `model.bindings.resourceSubType`: `Process` (rpa), `Agent` (agent), `Flow` (flow), `ProcessOrchestration` (agentic-process), `Api` (api-workflow), or the app type for HITL.
554	
555	**Why this is required.** The definition's `model.context[].value` fields are placeholders of the form `<bindings.{name}>` — deliberately invalid as runtime expressions, so they can't be confused with one. Before the BPMN is emitted, the runtime rewrites each placeholder to `=bindings.<id>` by finding a workflow-level binding with `(resourceKey, name)` matching the node's manifest `model.bindings.resourceKey` + the placeholder name. Without matching entries in top-level `bindings[]`, `uip maestro flow debug` fails with "Folder does not exist or the user does not have access to the folder" even though `uip maestro flow validate` passes.
556	
557	**Script:** `python3 scripts/check_bindings.py <flow>` reads each resource node's definition (`model.bindings.resourceKey` / `resourceSubType` and the `<bindings.NAME>` placeholders in `model.context[]`) and reports every missing `(resourceKey, name)` entry, plus duplicates and unused entries. `--emit` prints the missing entries as JSON; `--apply` appends them to the flow and refuses when the definition does not supply `resource` / `resourceSubType` — in that case take the exact shape from the resource plugin's `impl.md`.
558	
559	**Definitions stay verbatim.** Do NOT rewrite `<bindings.*>` placeholders inside the `definitions` entry — the definition is the authoring template. See "Every node type needs a `definitions` entry" in [author/CAPABILITY.md](../author/CAPABILITY.md).
560	
561	See each resource plugin's `impl.md` for the full JSON per node type: [rpa](../author/references/plugins/rpa/impl.md), [agent](../author/references/plugins/agent/impl.md), [flow](../author/references/plugins/flow/impl.md), [agentic-process](../author/references/plugins/agentic-process/impl.md), [api-workflow](../author/references/plugins/api-workflow/impl.md), [hitl](../author/references/plugins/hitl/impl.md).
562	
563	**Not to be confused with `bindings_v2.json`.** That file holds connector connection bindings for Integration Service nodes — a separate system. A flow may have both: a top-level `bindings[]` for resource references and a `bindings_v2.json` file for connector connections.
564	
565	## Bindings — connector connection binding
566	
567	When a flow uses connector nodes, the runtime needs to know **which authenticated connection** to use for each connector. This is configured in `content/bindings_v2.json`.
568	
569	See the relevant node guide in `nodes/` for the full `bindings_v2.json` schema, connection resource field reference, JSON examples, and the connection fetching workflow.
570

1	# HTTP Request Node — Manual Mode
2	
3	Use this walkthrough when there is no IS connector for the target service, the API needs no auth (or auth you pass yourself in headers), or you are prototyping against an arbitrary REST endpoint. For connector-managed auth, use [impl-connector.md](impl-connector.md) instead.
4	
5	**No connection lookup required.** Manual mode uses `ImplicitConnection` — there are no IS bindings.
6	
7	Before starting, read [impl.md](impl.md) for the node type, registry validation, and the "always use `node configure`" rule. Follow Steps 1–4 in order.
8	
9	## Step 1 — Add the node
10	
11	```bash
12	uip maestro flow node add <ProjectName>.flow core.action.http.v2 \
13	  --label "<HTTP node label>" --output json
14	```
15	
16	> **Inside a loop body?** Add `--parent <LOOP_NODE_ID>` to set `parentId`. Without it, the node runs outside the loop context and outputs are null. See [loop/impl.md](../loop/impl.md).
17	
18	The CLI copies the manifest into `definitions[]`, adds the node instance, registers `variables.nodes`, and inserts a `layout.nodes` placeholder — byte-for-byte from the registry. Save the returned `<nodeId>` — Step 2 reuses it. Leave `inputs` empty; Step 2 populates `inputs.detail`. Do not hand-author the definition — see [impl.md — Add the node](impl.md#add-the-node).
19	
20	## Step 2 — Configure the node
21	
22	> **Find missing values first.** Before composing `url` / `query` / `body`, resolve any values the agent doesn't have (IDs from names, required body fields, response shape, …). See [/uipath:uipath-platform — http-request.md](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/http-request.md).
23	
24	```bash
25	uip maestro flow node configure <ProjectName>.flow <nodeId> \
26	  --detail '{
27	    "authentication": "manual",
28	    "method": "GET",
29	    "url": "https://api.example.com/endpoint",
30	    "query": {"param1": "value1"}
31	  }' --output json
32	```
33	
34	The CLI:
35	
36	- Builds the full `inputs.detail` (manual auth, `ImplicitConnection`, bodyParameters, essentialConfiguration)
37	- Does **not** generate `bindings_v2.json` or a connection resource file — manual mode needs neither
38	
39	`url` must be a full URL (scheme + host + path). For auth headers you control, pass them under `headers`:
40	
41	```bash
42	uip maestro flow node configure <ProjectName>.flow <nodeId> \
43	  --detail '{
44	    "authentication": "manual",
45	    "method": "GET",
46	    "url": "https://api.example.com/me",
47	    "headers": {"Authorization": "=js:`Bearer ${$vars.apiToken}`"}
48	  }' --output json
49	```
50	
51	**Dynamic values:** HTTP input fields do not resolve `{$vars.x}` brace-templates — use `=js:` expressions for any dynamic `url` / `headers` / `body` / `query`. Pass the `=js:` string verbatim in `--detail`. Full rationale and examples: [impl.md — Dynamic values](impl.md#dynamic-values-in-url--headers--body--query).
52	
53	## Step 3 — (Optional) Response branches
54	
55	Skip unless you need to route downstream paths based on response content (e.g., `items.length > 0` vs empty). For generic call-failure handling use the `error` port in Step 4 instead. Full syntax and rules: [impl.md — Conditional branches](impl.md#conditional-branches).
56	
57	## Step 4 — Wire edges
58	
59	The HTTP node's target port is `input`. Source ports: `default` (success), `error` (network/non-2xx), `branch-{id}` (one per Step 3 entry). Wire `default` to the next node. Wire `error` to a handler **only when the requirements say what a failed call should do** — with no `error` edge the call faults the flow, which is the correct default, and setting `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true` without the edge swallows the failure into a run that reports success. See [file-format.md — Default: off](../../../../shared/file-format.md#default-off--enable-only-for-a-failure-the-flow-actually-handles).
60	
61	Edge JSON shapes and all four examples (upstream→node, default→downstream, error→handler, branch→downstream): [impl.md — Wire edges](impl.md#wire-edges).
62	
63	## Debug
64	
65	See [impl.md — Debug](impl.md#debug). For manual mode, watch for `ImplicitConnection` errors — they signal a missing `authentication: "manual"` flag or a non-URL `url` value.
66

1	# Script Node — Implementation
2	
3	## Node Type
4	
5	`core.action.script`
6	
7	## Registry validation
8	
9	```bash
10	uip maestro flow registry get core.action.script --output json
11	```
12	
13	Confirm: input port `input`, output port `success`, required input `script` (string, non-empty). See [Action Node Structure — Registry validation](../../../../shared/action-nodes.md#registry-validation) for the shared pattern.
14	
15	## JSON structure
16	
17	Follow the [Action Node Structure — Standard JSON skeleton](../../../../shared/action-nodes.md#standard-json-skeleton). The script-specific input is a single `script` string:
18	
19	```json
20	{
21	  "inputs": {
22	    "script": "const items = $vars.fetchData.output.body.items;\nconst total = items.reduce((sum, i) => sum + i.amount, 0);\nreturn { total, count: items.length };"
23	  }
24	}
25	```
26	
27	## Adding and editing
28	
29	See [Action Node Structure — Adding and editing procedures](../../../../shared/action-nodes.md#adding-and-editing-procedures). The script node uses the standard input port `input` and output port `success`; no plugin-specific wiring.
30	
31	## Script rules
32	
33	1. **Top-level body — no `function main()` wrapper.** Node runs the `script` text directly (as a function body); a wrapper is never called → `output` null. Read workflow variables via `$vars.<variableId>` and upstream node outputs via `$vars.<nodeId>.output`; end with top-level `return {…}`. Not a coded Function: no `main`, no injected args.
34	   - Correct: `const n = $vars.ixp1.output.field; return { n };`
35	   - Wrong: `function main({ ixp1 }) { … }`
36	2. **Must `return` an object** — `return { key: value }`, not a bare scalar. The return value becomes `$vars.<nodeId>.output`.
37	3. **`$vars` is a global** — use it directly: `return { upper: $vars.customerName.toUpperCase() }`
38	4. **JavaScript ES2020 (Jint engine)** — see [variables-and-expressions.md](../../../../shared/variables-and-expressions.md) for supported features and Jint constraints.
39	5. **No `console.log`** — `console` is not available. Use `return { debug: value }` to inspect values.
40	6. **No external calls** — use the HTTP node or a connector node for API calls.
41	7. **30-second timeout** — long-running computations will be killed.
42	8. **Never name a variable `aggregate`** — reserved host global. On any `Identifier 'X' has already been declared`, rename `X`.
43	
44	**Script:** `python3 scripts/lint_jint.py <ProjectName>.flow` checks rules 1, 2, 5, 6 and 8 above (plus the wider unsupported-construct list) across every script node and `=js:` expression in the file. The 30-second timeout is a runtime property and is not statically checkable.
45	
46	## Common patterns
47	
48	### Transform and return
49	
50	```javascript
51	const items = $vars.fetchData.output.body.items;
52	const filtered = items.filter(i => i.status === "active");
53	return { items: filtered, count: filtered.length };
54	```
55	
56	### Build a payload for a downstream node
57	
58	```javascript
59	return {
60	  subject: `Order ${$vars.orderId} - Confirmation`,
61	  body: `Your order of ${$vars.orderTotal} has been processed.`,
62	  recipient: $vars.customerEmail
63	};
64	```
65	
66	### Error check from upstream
67	
68	```javascript
69	const error = $vars.httpCall.error;
70	if (error) {
71	  return { hasError: true, message: error.message };
72	}
73	return { hasError: false, data: $vars.httpCall.output.body };
74	```
75	
76	### Reading a file-typed variable
77	
78	A `file` variable (bound via `uip maestro flow debug --attachment <id>=<path>`) hydrates as an **object**, not a string. Read the uploaded file's name from `.FullName`:
79	
80	```javascript
81	const doc = $vars.start.output.inputDoc; // file variable → object
82	return { fileName: doc.FullName };        // .FullName, not .name/.fileName
83	```
84	
85	Property access is **case-sensitive** — these casings resolve: `.FullName`, `.ID` (uppercase, not `.Id`), `.MimeType`, `.Metadata.size` (nested, lowercase `size`). `.name` / `.fileName` do not exist. See [variables-and-expressions.md — Runtime shape of a `file` variable](../../../../shared/variables-and-expressions.md#file-input).
86	
87	## Debug
88	
89	| Error | Cause | Fix |
90	| --- | --- | --- |
91	| Script did not return a value | Missing `return` statement | Add `return { ... }` |
92	| `output` is `null` but script has a `return` | `return` is inside an uncalled `function main(){}` wrapper | Remove wrapper; code + `return` at top level (rule 1) |
93	| Return value is not an object | Returned a scalar (`return 42`) | Wrap in object: `return { value: 42 }` |
94	| `$vars.nodeId` is undefined | Upstream node not connected or wrong ID | Check edges and node IDs |
95	| Timeout after 30s | Script too expensive | Simplify logic or split into multiple scripts |
96	| `console is not defined` | Used `console.log()` | Remove — use `return { debug: val }` instead |
97	| `fetch is not defined` | Tried to make HTTP call | Use an HTTP node or connector node instead |
98	| `[300501] Error invoking script task` with `Unexpected token` | Malformed JavaScript — `flow validate` does not parse script bodies, so syntax errors surface only at runtime. Common slip: one missing `)` in chained `(((a \|\| {}).b \|\| {}).c \|\| [])` guards | Balance parentheses; check with `node -e "new Function(<script>)"` before validate |
99	| `Identifier 'X' has already been declared` | `X` collides with a runtime-injected global (known: `aggregate`) | Rename `X` (e.g. `agg`) |
100

1	# Flow Editing Operations — CLI Carve-Outs
2	
3	This is **not** a structural editing guide. Use direct `.flow` authoring via [editing-operations-json.md](editing-operations-json.md) for OOTB node/edge/variable CRUD, trigger swaps, output mapping, subflows, inline-agent node/wiring, non-connector resources, and in-place updates.
4	
5	> **When to use this file:** only for CLI-managed carve-outs documented by a plugin: connector activities, connector triggers, and managed HTTP nodes (both `node add` and `node configure`). If you landed here while adding/removing/wiring OOTB nodes, inline-agent nodes, non-connector resources, or other structural graph elements, go back to the Edit / Write guide.
6	
7	The primitive commands below are support commands for carve-out workflows only. They are not an opt-in path for non-carve-out structural edits.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## Primitive Commands for Carve-Out Workflows
12	
13	### Add a node
14	
15	```bash
16	uip maestro flow node add <ProjectName>.flow <node-type> --output json \
17	  --input '<INPUT_JSON>' \
18	  --label "<LABEL>" \
19	  --position <X>,<Y> \
20	  --parent <PARENT_NODE_ID>
21	```
22	
23	**What the CLI handles automatically:**
24	- Inserts node into `nodes` array with a generated `id`
25	- Copies the definition from the local registry cache into `definitions` (one per unique type)
26	- Adds node output variables to `variables.nodes`
27	
28	**Flags:**
29	
30	| Flag | Required | Description |
31	|------|----------|-------------|
32	| `--input` | No | JSON object of node-specific inputs (expression, script, URL, etc.). Omit for nodes with no inputs (merge, end, terminate). |
33	| `--label` | No | Display label shown on the canvas |
34	| `--position` | No | `x,y` coordinates. Any value is fine (e.g. `0,0`) — `flow format` rewrites positions on save. |
35	| `--parent` | No | ID of an existing container node (e.g. a `core.logic.loop`). Sets `parentId` on the new node, placing it inside that container. Required for every node in a loop body — see [loop/impl.md](plugins/loop/impl.md). |
36	| `--output json` | Yes (for parsing) | Structured JSON response with the assigned node `id` |
37	
38	**Shell quoting tip:** If `--input` JSON contains special characters (quotes, braces, `$vars`), write it to a temp file and pass `--input "$(cat /tmp/input.json)"`.
39	
40	### Remove a node
41	
42	```bash
43	uip maestro flow node remove <ProjectName>.flow <NODE_ID>
44	uip maestro flow node remove <ProjectName>.flow <NODE_ID> --output json
45	```
46	
47	**What the CLI handles automatically:**
48	- Removes the node from `nodes`
49	- Removes all connected edges
50	- Removes orphaned definitions (definitions no longer referenced by any node)
51	- Removes orphaned bindings (connector bindings are shared at the connector level — a binding is only orphaned when no remaining node uses that connector)
52	- Removes node variables from `variables.nodes`
53	
54	### List nodes
55	
56	```bash
57	uip maestro flow node list <ProjectName>.flow --output json
58	```
59	
60	Returns all nodes with their `id`, `type`, and `display.label`. Use this to discover node IDs before wiring edges or removing nodes.
61	
62	### Add an edge
63	
64	```bash
65	uip maestro flow edge add <ProjectName>.flow <SOURCE_NODE_ID> <TARGET_NODE_ID> --output json \
66	  --source-port <PORT> \
67	  --target-port <PORT>
68	```
69	
70	**What the CLI handles automatically:**
71	- Inserts edge into `edges` array with a generated `id`
72	- Sets `targetPort` (required — validate rejects edges without it)
73	
74	See each plugin's `planning.md` or [file-format.md — Standard ports](../../shared/file-format.md) for port names by node type.
75	
76	### Remove an edge
77	
78	```bash
79	uip maestro flow edge remove <ProjectName>.flow <EDGE_ID>
80	uip maestro flow edge remove <ProjectName>.flow <EDGE_ID> --output json
81	```
82	
83	### List edges
84	
85	```bash
86	uip maestro flow edge list <ProjectName>.flow --output json
87	```
88	
89	Returns all edges with `id`, `sourceNodeId`, `sourcePort`, `targetNodeId`, `targetPort`.
90	
91	### Configure a connector node
92	
93	After adding a connector node with `node add`, configure it with connection details:
94	
95	```bash
96	uip maestro flow node configure <ProjectName>.flow <NODE_ID> \
97	  --detail '<DETAIL_JSON>'
98	```
99	
100	**What the CLI handles automatically:**
101	- Populates `inputs.detail` (connectionId, method, endpoint, bodyParameters, etc.)
102	- Creates connection binding entries in `bindings_v2.json`
103	- Creates connection resource files under `resources/solution_folder/connection/`
104	
105	The `--detail` JSON schema differs between connector activity nodes, connector trigger nodes, and managed HTTP nodes — see [connector/impl.md](plugins/connector/impl.md), [connector-trigger/impl.md](plugins/connector-trigger/impl.md), and [http/impl.md](plugins/http/impl.md) for the exact fields.
106	
107	**Shell quoting tip:** For complex `--detail` JSON, write it to a temp file:
108	
109	```bash
110	uip maestro flow node configure <file> <nodeId> --detail "$(cat /tmp/detail.json)" --output json
111	```
112	
113	### Configure a managed HTTP node
114	
115	After adding a `core.action.http.v2` node, configure it with target connector and connection details:
116	
117	```bash
118	uip maestro flow node configure <ProjectName>.flow <NODE_ID> \
119	  --detail '{
120	    "authentication": "connector",
121	    "targetConnector": "<TARGET_CONNECTOR_KEY>",
122	    "connectionId": "<TARGET_CONNECTION_ID>",
123	    "folderKey": "<FOLDER_KEY>",
124	    "method": "GET",
125	    "path": "/api/endpoint",
126	    "query": {"param1": "value1"}
127	  }'
128	```
129	
130	**What the CLI handles automatically:**
131	- Wraps your fields into the full `inputs.detail` structure (connector: `uipath-uipath-http`, bodyParameters, configuration)
132	- Generates `bindings_v2.json` with the target connector's connection
133	- Creates a connection resource file under `resources/solution_folder/connection/`
134	
135	See [http/impl.md](plugins/http/impl.md) for the full configuration workflow and JSON structure.
136	
137	### Validate
138	
139	```bash
140	uip maestro flow validate <ProjectName>.flow --output json
141	```
142	
143	Run **once** after all nodes, edges, and configuration are complete. Do not validate after each individual edit — intermediate states are expected to be invalid.
144	
145	---
146	
147	## Carve-Out Composite Operations
148	
149	These combine primitives only for workflows that are themselves carve-outs. Do not use them for non-carve-out structural edits; use [editing-operations-json.md](editing-operations-json.md) instead.
150	
151	### Replace manual trigger with connector trigger
152	
153	1. Remove the manual trigger (also removes its edges and orphaned definition):
154	   ```bash
155	   uip maestro flow node remove <ProjectName>.flow start --output json
156	   ```
157	2. Add the connector trigger node:
158	   ```bash
159	   uip maestro flow node add <ProjectName>.flow <TRIGGER_NODE_TYPE> \
160	     --label "<LABEL>" --position 200,144 --output json
161	   ```
162	3. Re-wire edge from the new trigger to the next node:
163	   ```bash
164	   uip maestro flow edge add <ProjectName>.flow <NEW_TRIGGER_ID> <NEXT_NODE_ID> \
165	     --source-port output --target-port input --output json
166	   ```
167	4. Configure the trigger with connection and event parameters:
168	   ```bash
169	   uip maestro flow node configure <ProjectName>.flow <NEW_TRIGGER_ID> --detail '<TRIGGER_DETAIL_JSON>'
170	   ```
171	
172	See [connector-trigger/impl.md](plugins/connector-trigger/impl.md) for the full `--detail` schema.
173	
174	---
175	
176	## Operations Not Supported by CLI
177	
178	These operations require the `Edit` tool. Use the [Edit / Write strategy guide](editing-operations-json.md) for:
179	
180	1. **Any non-carve-out structural edit** — node/edge CRUD, scheduled triggers, HITL QuickForm nodes, inline-agent nodes, non-connector resources, and graph rewiring
181	2. **Node input updates** — the CLI does not have a `node update` command; use `Edit` to preserve node IDs and `$vars.{nodeId}` references
182	3. **Workflow variables** — add/remove/update `variables.globals`
183	4. **Variable updates** — add/modify `variables.variableUpdates` entries
184	5. **Output mapping on End nodes** — add `outputs` object with `source` expressions
185	6. **Subflows** — create `subflows.{nodeId}` with nested nodes, edges, variables

Each subcommand touches every array the operation implies (nodes, edges, definitions,
variables.nodes, variables.variableUpdates, layout.nodes) in one pass and writes the file
back with 2-space indent.

                        edges/variables/updates/layout/definition
    add-edge            add an edge with both ports; sets errorHandlingEnabled
                        for error edges
    delete-edge         remove an edge by id or by endpoints
    set-input           in-place inputs update (dotted key path), preserves
                        node id
    add-variable        declare a workflow variable in variables.globals
    add-output-mapping  map an out variable on an End/terminate node
    add-variable-update

commands.result_summary:
uip maestro flow node configure                         
Configure a connector or managed HTTP node with connection and method details.
Run this after 'node add' — populates inputs.detail and creates workflow bindings.
Use 'node list' to find the node ID.

CONNECTOR ACTIVITIES (type uipath.connector.*, NOT *.trigger.*)
  Required: connectionId, folderKey, method, endpoint.
  Generic activities (manifest activityType='Generic', e.g. *.insert-record,
    *.list-records) also require objectName. Discover with:
      uip is resources list <connector-key> --operation <op> --connection-id <uuid>
      uip is resources describe <connector-key> <object> --operation <op> --connection-id <uuid>
  Curated activities: get method/endpoint from connectorMethodInfo in 'registry get'.
  Optional: bodyParameters, queryParameters, pathParameters, filter,
            customFieldsRequestDetails ({ objectActionName, parameterValues: [[k,v],...] });
  Examples:
    --detail '{"connectionId":"<uuid>","folderKey":"<uuid>","method":"POST","endpoint":"/issues","bodyParameters":{"summary":"Bug"}}'
    --detail '{"connectionId":"<uuid>","folderKey":"<uuid>","method":"POST","endpoint":"/Account","objectName":"Account","bodyParameters":{"Name":"Acme"}}'
  Cross-node bindings (referencing another node's output) require the
  "$vars." prefix inside the "=js:" expression — the bare form
  (e.g. "=js:createEntityRecord1.output.Id") resolves to undefined at runtime:
    --detail '{"connectionId":"<uuid>","folderKey":"<uuid>","method":"POST","endpoint":"/Account","bodyParameters":{"recordId":"=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"}}'

CONNECTOR TRIGGERS (type uipath.connector.trigger.*)
  Required: connectionId, folderKey, eventMode (e.g. 'polling' or 'webhook').
  Generic triggers (manifest activityType='GenericTrigger', e.g. Data Fabric
    *.record-created) also require objectName — the object to subscribe to.
    Discover with: uip is triggers objects <connector-key> <eventType> --connection-id <uuid>
  Optional: eventParameters, queryParameters, pathParameters,
            filter (structured FilterTree, not a raw expression).
  Discover eventMode with:
    uip is triggers describe <connector-key> <eventType> <object> --connection-id <uuid>
  Examples:
    --detail '{"connectionId":"<uuid>","folderKey":"<uuid>","eventMode":"polling"}'
    --detail '{"connectionId":"<uuid>","folderKey":"<uuid>","eventMode":"webhooks","objectName":"MyEntity"}'

CONNECTOR WAIT-FOR EVENTS (type uipath.connector.event.*)
  Mid-flow Receive Task that pauses execution until the event fires.
  Same detail shape as connector triggers — only activityType differs internally.
  Required: connectionId, folderKey, eventMode (e.g. 'polling' or 'webhooks').
  Generic event nodes also require objectName (same rule as triggers).
  Optional: eventParameters, queryParameters, pathParameters,
            filter (structured FilterTree, not a raw expression).
  Discover eventMode with:
    uip is triggers describe <connector-key> <eventType> <object> --connection-id <uuid>
  Example:
    --detail '{"connectionId":"<uuid>","folderKey":"<uuid>","eventMode":"polling","queryParameters":{"repo":"cli"}}'

MANAGED HTTP NODES (type core.action.http.v2)
  Two authentication modes — set via the 'authentication' key:

  Connector mode (authentication='connector'):
    Uses an Integration Service connection for auth.
    Required: authentication, method (GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE/OPTIONS/HEAD),
              connectionId (target connector connection UUID),
              folderKey, targetConnector (e.g. uipath-microsoft-outlook365)
    Optional: url (path appended to connector base URL), headers, query, body
    Example:
      --detail '{"authentication":"connector","targetConnector":"uipath-microsoft-outlook365","connectionId":"<uuid>","folderKey":"<uuid>","method":"GET","url":"/me"}'

  Manual mode (authentication='manual'):

content_blocks.text: Good, using **InvoiceIXP** and the file-created trigger. Let me check the connector-trigger and HTTP plugin docs for how to handle configuration when there's no live SharePoint/SAP connection yet.

I found an existing SharePoint/OneDrive connection in the tenant (`Productivity O365 OneDrive`, owned by a different user, folder `Shared`). Since that's not your SharePoint site's "New Vendor" folder and you explicitly asked me not to wire to live accounts, I won't bind it — I'll land the trigger node structurally and leave connection/folder as placeholders for IT. I'll use it only as a read-only schema reference to make sure the placeholder shape is accurate. Now scaffolding the solution and project.

Solution and flow scaffolded, trigger and HTTP node added. Now let me fetch the `core.control.end` definition and read the current flow file to author the IXP node, script node (to shape the SAP payload), and wire all the edges.

The trigger only outputs file **metadata** (ID, FullName, URL, etc.) — not the actual file bytes needed for extraction. I need a "Download File" step between the trigger and the IXP node to fetch the attachment object IXP requires. Let me check that node's shape.
The auto-generated `outputs.output.source` is `=result.response`, but per the IXP impl.md the canonical literal requires `source: "=this"`. Let me fix that.

Taxonomy lookup isn't available for this shared model from the CLI (it's not in the tenant's own IXP project list), which is an expected gap per the skill's docs — the fallback is defensive field-name guessing with assumptions surfaced as Open Questions, which I've already built into the script. Now let's add the script, end nodes, and wire everything.
Now let's wire the edges: trigger → download → IXP → script → HTTP → end (success), plus error paths from download/IXP/HTTP to endFailure.

Per the skill's rule, error handling should stay off by default unless the user specified a failure behavior — you didn't, so I'll let failures fault the flow visibly (the correct default) rather than inventing an error path. Let me remove the now-unused `endFailure` node.
Now configure the HTTP node in manual mode with placeholder SAP URL/auth, and the SharePoint trigger with placeholder site/folder values.

Manual HTTP mode configured correctly — `ImplicitConnection` binding, no live SAP account needed. Now for the SharePoint trigger and Download File node, I'll follow the No-Live-Tenant/Planned Configuration path since we're deliberately not binding to a real "New Vendor" folder.

The trigger requires a **path parameter** `ParentDriveID` (the drive/site location) resolved via `EventFolderPicker`, plus an optional filter on `ParentID` (exact folder) and `Extension` (to restrict to PDFs) — all of which need IT's real SharePoint site/folder IDs. Since there's no live "New Vendor" folder in this tenant, I'll write the planned configuration to a sidecar file rather than fabricate IDs, per the skill's no-live-tenant procedure.
Now let's run the audit and validate/format.

Audit is clean — the layout warnings are expected pre-`flow format`, and the unused-binding infos are the empty stubs from unconfigured connector nodes (expected in no-live-tenant mode). Now validate and format.

That warning is expected — you explicitly asked for a **plain HTTP POST to a URL IT gives you**, not a curated SAP connector operation (the SAP connectors in this tenant are typed operations like BAPI/RFC calls or C4C entity CRUD, which don't fit "POST arbitrary invoice JSON to a webhook URL"). Manual HTTP mode is the correct choice here; I'll note this in the final report rather than switching. Now formatting.
Validate passes, format is clean, audit is clean. Everything checks out.

The Maestro Flow is built and validated. Here's the full picture:

## File location
`/work/output/artifacts/skill-flow-ixp-invoice-extraction-simulated/InvoiceAutomationSolution/InvoiceExtractionFlow/InvoiceExtractionFlow.flow`

## Flow topology
```
SharePoint Trigger → Download File → Extract Invoice Fields (InvoiceIXP) → Build SAP Payload (script) → HTTP POST to SAP → Done
```
1. **New Invoice PDF Added** (SharePoint trigger, `uipath-microsoft-onedrive.file-created`) — fires when a new file lands in the "New Vendor" location, filtered to `.pdf` and the exact folder
2. **Download Invoice PDF from SharePoint** — the trigger only carries file metadata, not bytes, so this fetches the actual PDF content the IXP node needs
3. **Extract Invoice Fields (InvoiceIXP)** — IXP extraction node bound to your InvoiceIXP model
4. **Build SAP Invoice Payload** (script) — maps extracted fields into the JSON schema below
5. **POST Invoice Data to SAP** (manual-mode HTTP) — sends the JSON body
6. **Done** — success end node

## Validation status
`flow validate`: **Valid**, one expected warning (SAP-keyword-vs-generic-HTTP — explained below). `audit_flow.py`: **clean**. `flow format`: run, layout normalized.

## SAP payload shape sent
```json
{
  "invoiceNumber": "...",
  "vendorName": "...",
